subject: Copywriting
title: The Five-Word Rule
description: A quick, practical guide to The Five-Word Rule.

hook.text: Subject lines with 5 words get 16% higher open rates than those with 10. Shorter subjects win the inbox war.

buildup.text: Mobile screens show 30-40 characters. Desktop shows 60. If the subject is too long, the key word gets cut off.

discovery.text: 'Your order is ready'—5 words, clear, actionable.

twist.text: Some long subjects work brilliantly. But they front-load the hook.

climax.text: The rule isn't 'always short'—it's 'always clear in five words.' If the first five words don't hook, the rest don't.

punchline.text: Five words to hook. The rest is optional. Front-load value.

quiz.question: How many characters do mobile screens typically show for subject lines?

details.summary: Research suggests that subject lines of approximately five words (30-40 characters) hit the sweet spot for open rates. Short subject lines display fully on mobile screens, communicate quickly, and mimic the brevity of personal emails rather than marketing messages.
details.whyItMatters: Mobile now accounts for 60%+ of email opens. Subject lines that get truncated on mobile lose their impact. Brevity ensures the full message is visible where most reading happens.
takeaways: Five-word subject lines consistently achieve high open rates
Mobile email clients truncate subject lines after 30-40 characters
Short subjects mimic personal emails and avoid looking like marketing

faq.question: Is the five-word rule absolute?
faq.answer: No — it is a guideline, not a hard rule. Longer subject lines can work when they carry specific, compelling promises. The real principle is that every word must earn its place. Five words forces economy of language that usually improves clarity.

faq.question: How does mobile affect subject line strategy?
faq.answer: Over 60% of emails are opened on mobile devices, which display only 30-40 characters of the subject line. Front-loading the most important words and keeping subjects short ensures the full message is visible. Desktop-optimized long subjects lose impact on mobile.
